chunks: And to Solomon We subjected the wind, its morning journey being a month and its evening journey a month; and We made flow for him a spring of molten brass; and among the jinn were some who worked before him by the leave of his Lord; and whoever of them turned aside from Our command, We made him taste the torment of the blazing fire.

key_terms.بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِ: by the leave of his Lord

ai.seo_question: What were the specific divine gifts and subjugated forces given to Prophet Solomon (AS) according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights Solomon’s unique prophetic authority, where the subjugation of natural elements and jinn served as divine signs (ayat) rather than mere magic, emphasizing their obedience to God’s will. The mention of the 'spring of brass' (Ayn al-Qitr) is often interpreted as a source of strength or a specific location, illustrating the tangible manifestation of divine power granted to the prophets. This narrative reinforces the concept of 'Ilm al-Ladunni' (divine knowledge) and the hierarchical order of creation, where jinn and humans alike are subject to God’s command through their respective prophets.
